additions.name: (仮称)江東区千石三丁目計画 — planned five-storey data-centre building, Sengoku 3-chome, Koto

status.summary: Koto City Council's agenda for the 16 October 2026 meeting of its Disaster Prevention and Urban Development Special Committee, posted by 9 October 2026, lists for continued deliberation six petitions on the data-centre construction plan in Sengoku 3-chome, including requests for its withdrawal and for third-party verification, so the plan is a current, publicly identified project in October 2026. Koto City's 25 June 2026 committee reference describes it: a five-storey, 51.4 m steel building of 22,640 m2 on a 9,478.42 m2 site at 江東区千石3丁目2番, with construction planned for July 2026 to March 2029; Tokyo's sign-notification list (published 15 October 2026) records the same plan, （仮称）江東区千石三丁目計画 新築工事, on lots 千石三丁目2-19, 20, 71 and 89 with principal use data centre, notified on 8 May 2026 with a planned start in early July 2026. Only announced is supported: no building confirmation, start of works or completed stage is recorded in these sources, the planned dates are forecasts, and no operator, capacity or IT load is published.

locator.precision: Area centroid of the 計画地 (planned building site) outline on Koto City's 25 June 2026 committee reference map, registered to GSI z18 standard-map tiles by a similarity fit on three corners of the surrounding block (residuals 2.1-3.1 m); the registered outline measures 9,405 m2 against the official 9,478.42 m2 site. It locates the planned data-centre site in the south-west of the block north of Sendaibori River Park, not a building footprint, entrance, surveyed lot boundary or construction extent.
locator.identity_review: The ward reference gives 江東区千石3丁目2番 with a 9,478.42 m2 site and maps the 計画地 between the block's west street and the road along Sendaibori River Park (仙台堀川公園), about 500 m north of the Koto City Office; Tokyo's list gives the lots as 千石三丁目2-19, 20, 71 and 89 (lot numbers, not residential-address blocks: GSI's residential point for 千石三丁目2番 is the block to the north, and the 2026 MOJ/AIGID Koto registry file has no parcels in 千石). On the GSI standard map and seamless photo the registered outline coincides with a paved lot bounded by an apartment complex to the north, a tree strip and a parking structure to the east, roadside buildings at the south-west and the park road to the south; its north-east corner falls 3.2 m from the lot corner on the photo (independent check). Registration details, control points and the traced outline are in the geometry-facts file.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The ward map prints no coordinates or datum and is a 200-ppi raster; the 2-3 m control residuals measure only the map-to-GSI fit, and hand tracing of the outline adds a few metres. GSI standard-map feature accuracy is not stated. Estimated within roughly 15 m of the site centroid; the site extends about 60 m from the point. Decimal places are arithmetic precision.

additions.distinctness_review: Screened on 23 October 2026 against all five tables (sites.csv, projects.csv, evidence.csv, source-records.json, identity-mapping.json) of verified_construction_core/2026-10-23-research-fiftythird, all sources/*-holds.json, the pending queue fragments and claims.tsv, for 千石, Sengoku, 江東区/Koto and 東陽 and for any coordinate within 2.5 km of the point. No Atlas record, hold, claim or pending fragment lies within 2.5 km or mentions the plan; the nearest Atlas site is CEC Tokyo No.2 at Sunshine 60 (10.7 km), then the Shiroi and Inzai campuses (25 km and more). Tokyo's list records a separate planned data centre at Shiohama 2-chome 483-17, 41 and 42 (Phase II of the 塩浜二丁目開発計画, about 1.7 km south-west, not in the Atlas) and the Ariake TK2 data centre (about 5 km south-west, held in this fragment); neither shares lots, name or site with this plan. News reports name the developers, but no official record does, so no party or alias is attached.
additions.successor_review: The council page and agenda for 16 October 2026 were captured on 23 October 2026; minutes and results of that meeting are not yet published. Tokyo's FY2026 April-September sign-notification list (published 15 October 2026) still records the plan, and Tokyo's ordinance requires withdrawal notices when a plan is abandoned. No building confirmation, construction-start notice, change of plan or withdrawal was found in the ward's data-centre pages, the council agenda pages or the Tokyo list. The planned start in July 2026 is a forecast and no works are asserted. The 9 October 2026 announcement observation is kept.

additions.site_identity_review: SI1 and SI2 are the two older buildings of SCSK's netXDC Inzai campus, the existing Atlas site curated:scsk-netxdc-inzai-campus (vcc-site-82a8dc81ee48bf577b42), whose only project is SI3 (curated:scsk-netxdc-inzai:si3). SCSK's 1 October 2026 report states that the netXDC Inzai campus has three data centres, SI1 to SI3, and the campus page lists Chiba Center (SI1), Chiba No.2 Center (SI2) and Chiba No.3 Center (SI3) under the same 印西キャンパス（SI）. The SI3 admission (28th update) explicitly left SI1 and SI2 unadmitted and its locator precision note already says they are not separately mapped. They are a new project on the existing campus, not a new site.
additions.name: SCSK netXDC Chiba Center (SI1) and Chiba No.2 Center (SI2) Existing Operations

status.summary: SCSK's dated operator report of 1 October 2026 on its netXDC Inzai campus in Inzai, Chiba, states in the present tense that the campus has three data centres, SI1 to SI3, within SCSK's netXDC data-centre service, and describes campus-level operating measures (generator noise mitigation with measured compliance and temperature monitoring of discharged heat). The campus page identifies SI1 as Chiba Center (opened 2002) and SI2 as Chiba No.2 Center (opened 2015). This records the two existing buildings as operating on 1 October 2026; it is the report date, not an opening date, inspection day or occupancy measurement, and no capacity or IT load is asserted for either building.

locator.identity_review: Reuses exactly the existing netXDC Inzai campus point of the SI3 project 400c245c-51e6-5b28-b91f-0c9f27dbaaae (140.1182405, 35.8091485), with its pinned geometry evidence f5507327-bede-5656-8fbd-6a81254c2bcf; the baseline project has no geometry-identity evidence, so none is pinned. The point is a named SI3 facility marker used as the campus locator, and its existing precision note states that SI1 and SI2 are not separately mapped: it locates the campus that contains SI1 and SI2, not either building.

additions.distinctness_review: Screened on 23 October 2026 against all five tables (sites.csv, projects.csv, evidence.csv, source-records.json, identity-mapping.json) of verified_construction_core/2026-10-23-research-fiftythird, all sources/*-holds.json, the pending queue fragments and claims.tsv, for SCSK, netXDC, SI1, SI2, 千葉センター, 千葉第2センター and any coordinate within 2 km of the campus point. Within 2 km the Atlas holds the SCSK site itself (0 km, SI3 project) and STT Tokyo Inzai Campus (1.76 km, STT Tokyo 1 existing operations, a different operator and property); IIJ Shiroi Data Center Campus lies just outside at 2.02 km. No Atlas project, hold, claim or pending fragment covers SI1 or SI2; the only SCSK mentions elsewhere are the SI3 records and a distance note in the jp-kanto-p1 fragment. SI1 and SI2 are combined in one project because the report names them only together as the campus's other data centres and no source gives either a separate dated status.
additions.successor_review: The SCSK report page was re-captured on 23 October 2026 and is byte-identical to the 15 October capture; the campus page is also unchanged. SCSK's 23 June 2026 notice transfers, with effect planned for 1 October 2026, the system-operation business of its Data Center Division's service-infrastructure department (described in the notice as data-centre operation business, with sales of JPY 891 million in the year ended March 2026) to the wholly owned subsidiary SCSK System Management; the notice does not mention the netXDC buildings or brand, and SCSK's 1 October report still presents the netXDC Inzai campus as SCSK's own. No closure, sale, refurbishment or other change for SI1 or SI2 was found. The 1 October 2026 operating observation is kept.
